overview: Skyworks Solutions designs, manufactures, and markets analog and mixed-signal RF semiconductors -- amplifiers, filters, switches, front-end modules and related components -- used primarily in smartphones, with a growing secondary business in automotive, infrastructure, data center, Wi-Fi, and industrial/IoT applications ('Broad Markets'). The company is headquartered in Irvine, California, and is one of the largest suppliers of RF front-end content for Apple's iPhone. Skyworks is in the process of combining with rival Qorvo in an approximately $22 billion cash-and-stock merger expected to close on or about October 5, 2026, which will create a larger, more diversified RF/analog semiconductor company retaining the Skyworks name.

business_model.summary: Skyworks earns revenue selling RF front-end modules and discrete components to smartphone OEMs (primarily Apple) and, in its Broad Markets segment, to automotive, infrastructure, data center, Wi-Fi/networking, defense, and industrial/IoT customers. Revenue is transactional/design-win-driven rather than subscription-based: once a chip is designed into a device generation, Skyworks earns revenue each unit shipped for the life of that product cycle, but each new device generation is a fresh competitive bid. Mobile has historically supplied 60-67% of revenue and is heavily tied to Apple's iPhone unit volumes and RF content share; Broad Markets (~33-42% of revenue and growing faster, +10-15% y/y in recent quarters) is more diversified across hundreds of customers.

revenue_streams.name: Broad Markets - automotive, infrastructure, data center, Wi-Fi, defense, IoT

business_model.customer_type: B2B - concentrated in a small number of large OEM customers (Apple is the single largest) for Mobile; broader base of industrial, automotive Tier-1, networking, and defense/aerospace customers for Broad Markets
business_model.geographic_mix: Revenue billed predominantly to Asia-based contract manufacturers and OEMs (China, Taiwan, South Korea) reflecting the global electronics supply chain, though end-demand is global; manufacturing/R&D concentrated in the US with assembly/test operations overseas

competitive_position.market_position: Top-3 to top-5 global RF front-end module supplier with roughly 5-6% global RFFE market share as of 2025, behind Qualcomm (~21% share, modem-RF integration strategy) and Broadcom (~18% share, FBAR filters and multi-year Apple supply agreements); Qorvo is a similarly-sized direct peer (~6% share) that Skyworks is in the process of acquiring/merging with to create a combined #2-3 player with greater scale

moat_factors.description: Once designed into a device platform, RF content tends to persist for that generation, but OEMs (especially Apple) can and do re-bid sockets each generation and increasingly dual-source, eroding this advantage

moat_factors.factor: Technology/IP in filters and PA modules
moat_factors.description: Deep expertise in SAW/BAW filters, power amplifiers and module integration required for 5G/Wi-Fi 7 complexity, but Broadcom's FBAR filter technology and Qualcomm's integrated modem-RF platform are structurally stronger in premium sockets
Combined Skyworks-Qorvo is expected to generate $500M+ in annual cost synergies and pro forma revenue of ~$7.7B, improving fab utilization and R&D leverage versus standalone scale
Deep, long-standing Apple relationship provided volume certainty for over a decade, but the same concentration is now actively working against Skyworks as Apple diversifies its supply base

weaknesses: Heavy reliance on a single customer (Apple) for the majority of revenue leaves Skyworks exposed to sourcing decisions outside its control
Loss of exclusive/majority RF socket share at Apple (dual-sourcing for iPhone 17, ~20-25% content loss) demonstrates limited pricing/relationship power versus the customer
Smaller R&D and capex budget than Qualcomm or Broadcom on a standalone basis, which the Qorvo merger is explicitly designed to address
Broad Markets diversification, while growing, is not yet large enough to offset Mobile declines at the revenue/margin level

growth_drivers: Qorvo merger (expected to close ~October 5, 2026) creating a combined ~$7.7B revenue company with greater scale, broader product portfolio, and $500M+ targeted annual cost synergies within 24-36 months

Broad Markets diversification into automotive (ADAS, connectivity), data center/networking, Wi-Fi 7, defense/aerospace, and industrial IoT -- grew Broad Markets revenue roughly 10% y/y with the three 'growth engine' categories (Wi-Fi, data center, automotive) up ~15% y/y in fiscal Q3 2026, with demand reportedly outstripping current supply
5G and Wi-Fi 7 content complexity increases dollar content per device even as unit growth is flat, benefiting suppliers who can integrate filters/PAs into higher-value modules
Defense/aerospace RF content (radar, EW, satellite communications) is a smaller but higher-margin, less cyclical growth vector, more relevant post-merger given Qorvo's defense exposure
Potential market share recovery or stabilization at Apple if dual-sourcing proves temporary or Skyworks wins back content in future iPhone generations
Post-merger cross-selling and combined customer relationships, particularly deepening non-Apple Mobile and Broad Markets accounts

business.description: Apple still represented roughly 57-63% of revenue through fiscal 2026; any shift in sourcing, pricing, or iPhone unit demand directly moves Skyworks' results. Apple's February 2026 decision to dual-source a premier RF socket for iPhone 17 (benefiting Qualcomm/Broadcom) caused an estimated 20-25% RF content loss and triggered sharp analyst downgrades and price target cuts

business.risk: Smartphone unit cycle / RF content competition
business.description: Global smartphone unit growth is roughly flat-to-low-single-digit; Skyworks must win RF content share each device generation against Qualcomm, Broadcom, Qorvo and emerging Chinese suppliers (MediaTek-ecosystem) rather than relying on market growth

Revenue fell from a ~$5.4-5.5B peak in FY2021-22 to roughly $4.0-4.1B in FY2024-25 and quarterly runs near $935M-$1.04B through FY2026, reflecting the post-pandemic smartphone upgrade slowdown compounded by the Apple content loss

business.risk: Customer-specific design loss risk extends beyond Apple
business.description: Broad Markets customers are more numerous but each individual design win/loss at a large automotive or networking OEM can still be material to segment growth

financial.description: The Qorvo deal issues significant new Skyworks stock (Qorvo holders to own ~37% of combined company) plus cash consideration ($32.50/share), creating near-term integration costs, potential incremental debt, and execution risk on achieving the targeted $500M+ synergies
Foreign-sourced raw materials (including from China) and international manufacturing/test operations create modest FX and input-cost exposure

regulatory.risk: China export controls / entity list restrictions
regulatory.description: Expanding US export restrictions and additions to the BIS Entity List have limited and could further limit Skyworks' ability to sell to certain Chinese entities and their business partners
2025-2026 US tariff actions and Chinese retaliatory countermeasures affect trade flows, costs, and demand given Skyworks' significant revenue billed through Asia-based supply chains
The merger received Qorvo and Skyworks shareholder approval (February 2026) and all necessary regulatory clearances were obtained by September 30, 2026, leaving limited remaining closing risk

regulatory.risk: China rare earth / materials export controls
regulatory.description: Broader 2026 Chinese rare-earth export controls pose industry-wide supply chain risk to semiconductor and electronics manufacturers, including RF component makers

macro.description: Mobile revenue is tied to discretionary consumer smartphone upgrade cycles, which are sensitive to macro/consumer spending conditions

macro.risk: Semiconductor capital equipment and capacity cycles
macro.description: RF front-end demand for growth engines (data center, Wi-Fi, automotive) is currently supply-constrained, a tailwind now but a capacity-driven margin risk if overbuilt

execution.description: Combining two large RF semiconductor organizations (manufacturing footprints, product roadmaps, customer relationships, and headcount) carries material execution risk; CEO Phil Brace leads the combined company with Qorvo's Bob Bruggeworth joining the board
Leadership team for the combined company was only recently announced; integration-related distraction or key talent attrition is a risk through the 2026-2027 integration window

macro_factors.industry_outlook: The global RF front-end module market is maturing in smartphones (flat-to-low-single-digit unit growth) but increasing in per-device dollar content due to 5G/Wi-Fi 7 complexity; faster growth is occurring in automotive RF/connectivity, data center/networking, and defense/aerospace RF applications, which are smaller but higher-growth end markets that the Skyworks-Qorvo combination is explicitly targeting
macro_factors.cyclicality: High in Mobile (tied to consumer smartphone upgrade cycles and a single large customer's design decisions); moderate-to-low in Broad Markets, which is more diversified across automotive, industrial, and infrastructure end markets
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct sensitivity (minimal net debt historically), but moderate indirect sensitivity via consumer discretionary spending on smartphones and enterprise capex cycles for networking/data center equipment; merger financing could introduce new debt-related rate sensitivity
key_input_costs: Gallium arsenide and other compound semiconductor wafers
Rare earth and specialty materials subject to Chinese export controls

recent_developments.event: Skyworks announced it received all necessary regulatory clearances for the Qorvo merger; close expected on or about October 5, 2026

Reported fiscal Q3 2026 results: revenue of $935M (above the ~$925.9M consensus), non-GAAP EPS of $1.08 (beat), non-GAAP operating income of $182M; Mobile revenue declined but Broad Markets grew with the Wi-Fi/data center/automotive 'growth engines' up a combined ~15% y/y; guided fiscal Q4 2026 revenue of $1.01-1.06B and EPS of approximately $1.27 at the midpoint
Qorvo and Skyworks shareholders each approved the merger and related proposals at special stockholder meetings

Apple decided to dual-source a premier RF socket for the iPhone 17, resulting in an estimated 20-25% RF content loss for Skyworks at Apple (benefiting Qualcomm and/or Broadcom); shares fell sharply (reported as high as a 25% single-day decline) and multiple analysts (Mizuho, Stifel, Argus) cut ratings/price targets, with some fair value estimates cut from ~$95-105 to ~$62-70

Skyworks and Qorvo announced a definitive merger agreement to combine in a cash-and-stock transaction valued at approximately $22 billion; Qorvo holders to receive 0.960 Skyworks shares plus $32.50 cash per share; pro forma ownership ~63% Skyworks / ~37% Qorvo; combined pro forma revenue of ~$7.7B and Adjusted EBITDA of ~$2.1B targeted, with $500M+ annual cost synergies expected within 24-36 months; Phil Brace (Skyworks CEO) to lead the combined company, Bob Bruggeworth (Qorvo CEO) to join the board; combined Apple revenue exposure expected to fall to roughly 45-55% of the combined company's revenue
Apple's share of Skyworks revenue declined from roughly 63% a year earlier to about 57% in fiscal Q3 2026, consistent with the iPhone 17 dual-sourcing content loss

items.notes: Sequential increase from Q3 FY2026's $935M, driven by seasonal Mobile strength and continued Broad Markets growth

items.vs_prior: raised vs. Q3 FY2026 actual of $1.08
items.notes: Reflects higher revenue and operating leverage expectations

items.metric: Broad Markets / growth engines (Wi-Fi, data center, automotive)
items.notes: Management noted demand for these products is running ahead of current supply capacity
Expected to be immediately EPS accretive; combined pro forma revenue ~$7.7B, Adjusted EBITDA ~$2.1B

items.target: 45-55% of combined company revenue (down from ~57-63% standalone)
items.vs_prior: new disclosure tied to merger rationale
items.notes: Key stated benefit of the Qorvo combination is reduced single-customer concentration

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Phil Brace characterized Q3 FY2026 as 'a solid quarter with revenue and earnings above expectations, reflecting consistent execution across the portfolio,' noting Mobile 'performed well on healthy demand' while Broad Markets delivered 'another quarter of year-over-year growth, led by double-digit gains in automotive and data center,' with growth-engine demand (Wi-Fi, data center, automotive) collectively up 15% y/y and running ahead of current supply. Management has emphasized the Qorvo combination as the primary strategic response to Apple concentration risk and RF industry cyclicality, targeting immediate EPS accretion and $500M+ in synergies.

bull_case: Qorvo merger (closing ~October 5, 2026) creates meaningful scale (~$7.7B pro forma revenue), diversifies Apple concentration down to an estimated 45-55% of combined revenue, and targets $500M+ in annual cost synergies with immediate EPS accretion
Broad Markets 'growth engines' (Wi-Fi, data center, automotive) are growing double digits with demand reportedly outstripping supply, providing a credible non-Apple growth vector

Stock trades at a depressed valuation after the iPhone 17 content-loss selloff, with a forward P/E well below the trailing P/E, suggesting the market may already price in most of the near-term Apple content loss
Combined Skyworks-Qorvo becomes a larger, more credible #2/#3 global RF front-end supplier with broader IP portfolio (filters, PAs, defense RF) and improved negotiating leverage with OEM customers
Industry-wide 5G/Wi-Fi 7 content complexity continues to raise RF dollar content per device even in a flat unit environment, a structural tailwind for the surviving large-scale RF suppliers
bear_case: Apple's move to dual-source RF content for iPhone 17 (an estimated 20-25% content loss) may be the start of a structural erosion of Skyworks' most important customer relationship rather than a one-time event, with further share loss possible in subsequent iPhone generations
Revenue has fallen roughly 25% from the FY2021-22 peak of ~$5.1-5.5B to roughly $4.0-4.1B in FY2024-25, and Mobile segment weakness continues to offset Broad Markets growth at the consolidated level

Large, complex merger integration with Qorvo carries meaningful execution risk -- combining manufacturing footprints, product roadmaps, and cultures -- with synergy targets not guaranteed to be realized on the stated 24-36 month timeline

Consensus analyst sentiment is lukewarm (mostly Hold ratings, price targets clustered around $64-$74, with multiple post-content-loss downgrades from firms including Mizuho, Stifel, and Argus cutting fair value estimates toward $62-$70)

Persistent China/US trade tensions, export controls (including Entity List restrictions and rare-earth controls), and tariff actions create ongoing supply chain and demand uncertainty for a company with significant revenue billed through Asia-based OEMs and contract manufacturers

Even post-merger, the combined company remains meaningfully smaller than Qualcomm and Broadcom in RF front-end share, and smartphone unit growth secularly remains flat-to-low-single-digit, capping the ceiling for the core Mobile business
